item.title: Canada’s monetary policy framework: A trusted anchor in uncertain waters

rating.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem outlines the renewed five-year monetary policy framework, reaffirming the 2% CPI inflation target and explaining how the Bank will navigate supply shocks in an increasingly uncertain global environment. He acknowledges that inflation has been running around 3% since April and that the Bank raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 2.5% in October due to persistent energy-driven cost pressures and resilient economic performance. The speech also introduces a new inflation dashboard and clarifies the role of core inflation measures as inputs rather than targets.
rating.stance_rationale: The speech has a mildly hawkish tilt: the Bank recently hiked 25bp and signaled concern about second-round effects from energy prices feeding into broader consumer prices, while noting the economy has been more resilient than expected. However, the overall tone is balanced and framework-focused rather than explicitly signaling further tightening.
key_quotes: The combination of increased inflation persistence and modestly better economic performance supported our decision in October to raise the policy interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%.
Our goal is to avoid a situation where Canadians face rising prices for a wide range of goods and services.
